logline: Hansal Mehta adapts journalist Jigna Vora's memoir about being accused of ordering a rival reporter's murder, tracing her arrest, imprisonment, and the media machinery that tried to bury her before truth emerged.

seasons.review_body: Hansal Mehta adapts Jigna Vora's memoir with the same instinct that made Scam 1992 work: anchoring systemic critique inside one person's lived ordeal. Jagruti Pathak, the crime reporter framed for ordering a murder, is carried by Karishma Tanna in a performance critics identified as the best of her career. The show is dense with period journalism detail, Mumbai crime beat texture, and the machinery of how institutions close ranks against inconvenient individuals. The RT score reflects a genuine consensus. The one reservation some critics raised is structural: the series is so invested in the procedural and institutional layers that its emotional centre occasionally feels secondary to the machinery around it.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.review_body: Scoop Season 1 Episode 1 released June 2, 2023 on Netflix as the premiere of the 6-episode series. Rotten Tomatoes holds Season 1 at 92 percent from 12 critics; IMDb audience scored the season 7.5. Hindustan Times wrote that Hansal Mehta 'sets the bar high in one of the best shows of the year.' The premiere establishes crime reporter Jagruti Pathak's professional world with precise period detail - the fax machines, the competitive journalist culture, the way scoops moved before digital. Hansal Mehta grounds her in a newsroom that functions as a system, not a backdrop, which makes her later fall from it feel institutional rather than personal. Karishma Tanna anchors every scene without melodrama, the register critics identified as the performance's key strength.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: Crime reporter Jagruti Pathak chases a serial bomb blast story and uncovers a lead that will consume her next three years. Hansal Mehta establishes the Mumbai crime beat with precise period detail - the fax machines, the press briefings, the way a story travels before Twitter.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Jagruti's first instinct that the story is bigger than the press release - the moment the show earns Karishma Tanna's career-best notice.

critic_note.text: Hansal Mehta sets the bar high in one of the best shows of the year.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 2
episode_reviews.review_body: Scoop Season 1 Episode 2 released June 2, 2023 on Netflix. The series holds 92 percent on Rotten Tomatoes from 12 critics; IMDb audience scored it 7.5. Hindustan Times described the show as 'one of the best shows of the year.' The second episode follows Jagruti on a Kashmir assignment before a major breaking story recalls her to Mumbai. Mehta uses the geographic interruption to establish how the crime beat functions under deadline pressure, and the episode advances the show's procedural machinery without yet triggering the crisis that will define it. The pacing is deliberate and trusting - consistent with Mehta's characteristic confidence that the architecture will sustain the audience.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: A trip to Kashmir is interrupted when a major story breaks; Jagruti is pulled back into the city and toward a case she does not yet know will destroy her career. The procedural mechanics are tight and Mehta's newsroom detail keeps the episode grounded in how journalism actually works.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The phone call summoning Jagruti back - the last moment before the machine closes around her.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 4
episode_reviews.review_body: Scoop Season 1 Episode 4 released June 2, 2023 on Netflix. The series holds 92 percent on Rotten Tomatoes; IMDb audience gave it 7.5. Hindustan Times described Mehta's direction as setting the bar for Indian OTT drama of the year. The fourth episode puts Jagruti in custody and lets the institutional mechanics of accusation play at full force. Mehta's sharpest argument about media complicity comes into view here: the same industry Jagruti served and understood is now producing her arrest as content, with the same competitive velocity it applies to every other story. Karishma Tanna's performance in custody - controlled fear rather than theatrical breakdown - is where her work locks in as the season's best.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: Jagruti is in custody and the institutional mechanisms of accusation are fully engaged. The episode is where the show's argument about media complicity becomes impossible to miss - the same industry Jagruti served is now producing her as content.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Jagruti watching her own arrest covered on the news channels - the show's sharpest self-reflexive image.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 6
episode_reviews.review_body: Scoop Season 1 Episode 6 released June 2, 2023 on Netflix as the series finale. The season holds 92 percent on Rotten Tomatoes from 12 critics. The Rotten Tomatoes consensus called it 'densely plotted yet character-driven.' The finale navigates Jagruti's path through the judicial machinery without manufacturing a cathartic courtroom triumph. Mehta's restraint is his signature: the resolution arrives not through a dramatic reversal but through the accumulation of evidence and the slow retreat of the institutional forces that opposed her. The closing sequence reflects on what the experience costs rather than celebrating what it resolves, which is the reason the series' overall argument about media and justice lands as substantial rather than polemical.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The finale navigates Jagruti's path through the judicial machinery toward an eventual truth, refusing the triumphalist arc the material invites. The restraint is Mehta's signature; the emotional payoff is earned rather than manufactured.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The final courtroom exchange - not a verdict but a small reckoning, exactly as understated as the season that built to it.
